note: Dominica, read on 2026-10-30 on the Invest Dominica Authority's Work & Residency Permit page (investdominica.com, the government's investment agency; its footer dated 2023) and the Government of Dominica's 'How Do I Apply for a Residence Permit?' (dominica.gov.dm). This replaces the file held in wave 8, whose work permit was read as tied to the employer and as applied for in Dominica, and whose residence permit was read as allowing no work: none of the three is written now. Non-nationals wishing to work must first obtain a work permit from the Labour Division; it is valid for one year and can be renewed, and confers residency status where the employment lasts more than six months. Its application fee is EC$800 for non-CARICOM nationals (written) and EC$250 for CARICOM members; the applicant's employer writes accepting responsibility and offering employment for a year in the first instance, and an extension of stay is required until the permit is approved; the page doesn't say in words what work the permit allows or where it is applied for, so neither is written. The residence permit (administered by the Ministry of National Security and Home Affairs) asks a banker's statement of the applicant's or a sponsor's finances and a letter from a friend, family member or sponsor accepting responsibility; the government's page says an applicant stays a visitor on an extension of stay recorded by the Immigration Department, without which they are on island illegally and get no form, so it is written as applied for in Dominica. It costs EC$800 for non-CARICOM nationals (EC$250 for CARICOM), is valid one year, renewable yearly up to five years, after which the applicant can receive permanent residency (5 written). Its purpose isn't named beyond residence; it is written as the means route, the applicant's finances being its test (a reading). The terms of permanent residency, its fee, decision times and the years to naturalisation aren't stated (the page's sentence on two years as a permanent resident is cut off). OECS citizens' freedom to work is the work engine's, not read here.

sources.title: Invest Dominica Authority, Work & Residency Permit
sources.said: Non Nationals wishing to engage in work in Dominica must first obtain a work permit from the Labour Division. ... A work permit automatically confers residency status if the term of employment lasts for more than six months. All work permits are valid for one-year duration and can be renewed. ... accepting responsibility for employee; and offer of employment for one year in the first instance ... Application fee: EC$800.00 US$295.00 (Non-CARICOM Members) OR EC$250.00 US$93.00 (CARCOM) ... Extension of stay is required until permit is approved ... Letter from applicant’s friend/family accepting responsibility for applicant while in Dominica. ... The Ministry responsible for administering residence permits is the Ministry of National Securityand Home Affairs. All residence permits are valid for one-year duration and can be renewed on a yearly basis for a period up to five years after which time the applicant can receive permanent residency.

sources.title: Government of Dominica, How Do I Apply for a Residence Permit?
sources.said: Extension of Stay must be sought from the Immigration Department and recorded in the passport. Unless an applicant's immigration status changes to Work or Residence Permit, the applicant's status remains as visitor, and the application must have Extension of Stay. If the applicant does not apply for Extension of Stay he/she is on island illegally, and will not be given an application form until his/her status of visitor is regularized. ... Statement of financial position from a reputable banker from the applicant or person accepting responsibility for the applicant. ... Non-CARICOM Nationals: EC$800.00
